standard.title: Move safely and expressively
standard.description: experiment with ways to move safely and expressively using fundamental movement skills and the elements of dance
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have used play and imagination to discover movement possibilities at Foundation. They can vary movement in simple ways and are building awareness of their body in space.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students experiment with ways to move safely and expressively using fundamental movement skills and the elements of dance.

nodes.label: Safe dance awareness
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe and practise safe dance — being aware of self and others in the space, moving with care, and taking responsibility for their own physical wellbeing.
nodes.minimum_width: Consistent demonstration of spatial awareness and care for self and others during movement activities in a defined space.
nodes.typical_width: Developing responsibility for safe dance practice: awareness of self and others in the space; recognising the boundaries of the dance space; understanding body care (hydration, rest); moving safely in open and crowded spaces; using props such as scarves without endangering others.
wider: Reflect explicitly on moments of safe and unsafe movement — discussing what made movement feel safe or risky and identifying strategies
Practise safe movement in varied spatial configurations — small groups, scattered, lines — building adaptable spatial awareness
nodes.hinge_reason: Safe dance awareness is a prerequisite for all physical engagement in dance. Students who do not internalise spatial awareness and body care cannot participate safely in subsequent technical or expressive movement work.

response_modes.reason: Safe practice must become habitual — not a checklist that requires conscious effort. Repeated practice across many sessions builds the automatic awareness and responsibility that safety in dance requires.

success_criteria: Student consistently maintains awareness of others in the dance space during movement activities
Student can describe at least one safe dance practice (e.g. checking space around them, landing softly)

nodes.label: Fundamental movement exploration
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore fundamental locomotor and non-locomotor movements expressively — varying level, direction, size and quality in response to prompts.
nodes.minimum_width: Practising at least four fundamental movements (e.g. running, jumping, rolling, skipping) — varying one element (e.g. level or speed) in each.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring fundamental locomotor movements (running, skipping, rolling, jumping, walking backwards, sideways movements) and non-locomotor movements; using improvisation to explore movement possibilities in response to stimuli (imagery, music, stories); making movements bigger, smaller, faster, slower, higher, lower.
wider: Explore movement inspired by familiar natural phenomena — falling like a leaf, gliding like a bird, rolling like a log — attending to dynamics and control
Improvise movements in response to Viewpoints questions: 'What levels are you using?', 'Can you use a different body part?', 'What direction could you travel?'

response_modes.reason: Students need broad physical repertoire — many movement types across many variations — before they can make expressive choices. Movement variety must be built before it can be deployed intentionally.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who explore fundamental movements across a wide range of dynamics, directions and qualities develop the physical vocabulary that supports genuine expressive choice in the Creating and Presenting strands.
success_criteria: Student demonstrates at least four fundamental locomotor movements
Student can vary a movement in at least two ways (e.g. change level AND change speed) when prompted

nodes.label: Expressive movement with elements
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can move expressively using fundamental skills and elements of dance — communicating ideas or feelings through movement quality.
nodes.minimum_width: One movement sequence using at least two elements to express an idea or feeling — student can explain what they are communicating.
nodes.typical_width: Using improvisation and element awareness to communicate expressively: contrasting dynamics (stamping heavily vs tip-toeing lightly), using movement qualities to express ideas (slow sinking = melting, sharp jerky = robot); applying Viewpoints questions to improve expressive clarity.
wider: Explore how the same idea (e.g. a weather event) can be expressed through contrasting element combinations — comparing expressive effect
Use Viewpoints questions to evaluate own expressive choices: 'How are you communicating your ideas?', 'What other body parts could you use?'

response_modes.reason: Expressive movement integrates safe body use (N1), physical vocabulary (N2), and element awareness (from C strand) into intentional communication. Connect back explicitly: 'You're moving safely AND communicating — that's expressive dance.'

success_criteria: Student uses movement quality (not just movement type) to communicate an idea — evident from observer's perspective
Student can identify what they are communicating through their movement
